title: Strideboard: composite model/route KPI panels and anomaly-first chart specs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and spec a new composite ‘Strideboard’ UI component that surfaces per-model and per-route inference KPIs (p50/p95 latency, throughput RPS, token rate, token-type mix, cost per 1K tokens) in a single horizontal strip. The Strideboard is intended for both the model detail page and the route overview page; it should be compact, scannable, and support quick drilling into time windows, percentiles, and anomaly flags. This ticket covers layout variants, charting rules, annotation semantics, and handoff assets for engineering (Figma frames + JSON chart specs).
acceptance_criteria: Strideboard designs completed for three breakpoints: desktop wide, desktop compact, and mobile stack
Chart spec documents define series, aggregation window, percentile bands, anomaly marker rules, and color tokens for positive/negative SLO delta
Token-type donut and cost-per-1k microcard are included and match backend telemetry fields (tokens_total, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, cost_usd_per_1000_tokens)
Handoff assets uploaded: Figma prototype link, Confluence spec with example queries, and a sample Chart JSON for frontend team
UX review signed off by Product and Observability eng leads
Accessibility checks: color contrast and keyboard interaction documented
design_notes: Primary use case is quick ops triage: user scans for anomalies (p95 spikes, token-rate jumps) then clicks to open timeline drill-in
Visual hierarchy: leftmost micro KPI (model name + active route), middle timeline with stacked percentile bands, rightmost set of microcards (throughput, tokens, cost)
Anomaly-first principle: small red dot appears inline on the timeline at first anomalous point; hover shows suggested action (open incident, rollback, reroute)
Percentile bands are rendered as 50/90/99 with semi-transparent fills; p50 line is solid, p95 dashed, p99 dotted
Cost overlay: toggleable layer that converts y-axis into cost-per-1k tokens; should be a secondary axis to avoid rescaling throughput charts
Token-type breakdown: donut shows prompt vs completion vs assistant tokens for selected window; clicking isolates timeline series to that token-type
Streaming vs batch indicator: small badge near route name to indicate serving mode; timeline aggregates differently for streaming (per-second) vs batching (per-request)
Compact mode collapses the timeline to a sparkline with percentile shading and shows KPIs stacked vertically
chart_spec_highlights: Time window presets: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d; default 24h for model detail, 6h for route overview
Aggregation: 10s buckets for <=1h, 1m buckets for <=24h, 5m for >24h; percentile computed over requests in the bucket
Percentile plotting: compute p50/p95/p99; draw p50 as #0F62FE, p95 as #FF8A00, p99 as #D0011B with opacity 0.08 fill between p50-p95 and p95-p99
Anomaly rule: point flagged if metric deviates >3 sigma from rolling baseline (24h medoid) OR relative change >40% from prior window
Tooltip: show absolute and relative delta to baseline, sample traces link if available, and estimated incremental cost for the spike
Microcard metrics: throughput (RPS avg+peak), token_rate (tokens/s), cost_per_1k (USD), errors_per_min; each microcard supports quick-compare (previous period delta)
Color tokens: success/green #0BA37F, warning/orange #FFB020, danger/red #D0011B; neutral gray #6F7681
Exportable CSV: timeline series for selected window with bucket timestamps and raw values (tokens_total, latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, requests)
Embeddable Chart JSON sample attached for the frontend visualization library used by Console (lightweight Vega-like format)
decisions: Use a single Strideboard component for both model and route pages to reduce cognitive overhead and development cost
Default to percentile bands + anomaly markers rather than only point-in-time alerts to better surface incipient regressions
Cost overlay is opt-in to avoid clutter for low-cost accounts
Token-type donut is contextual: hidden on route list but visible on model detail and route detail
